speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the dizziness as a spinning sensation (vertigo) or just feeling lightheaded? Also, do these episodes happen with specific head movements or are they constant?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the detailed description. To help differentiate between benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) and other causes like vestibular neuritis or stroke, have you noticed any associated symptoms such as hearing loss in one ear, tinnitus (ringing), or weakness on one side of your body during these episodes?

Also, please tell me if anyone has performed the Dix-Hallpike maneuver for you to confirm the specific head movements that trigger the spinning sensation.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the clarification. Since you mentioned age-related hearing loss but denied recent unilateral hearing loss, I need to rule out central causes. Has this dizziness ever been accompanied by double vision, slurred speech, or numbness in your limbs?

REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver. REQUEST IMAGES: Head_MRI if symptoms were atypical or persistent.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dix-Hallpike Manoeuvre: Positive for right-sided horizontal nystagmus when moving from sitting to supine position, suggestive of BPPV; MRI Brain: No evidence of central lesions or infarcts.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. No history of Meniere's disease, vestibular neuritis, or labyrinthitis. Social history: Retired school teacher. Lives alone. Non-smoker, occasional wine. Enjoys light gardening.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headache, tinnitus, hearing loss, nausea, vomiting, or recent respiratory infections. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is an interesting observation from your previous doctor, as typical migraine vertigo usually lasts longer than the seconds-long episodes you described with position changes. To clarify the diagnosis between BPPV and vestibular migraine, has your family or a physician ever observed nystagmus (involuntary eye jerking) when you turn your head or lie down? Also, do you have a history of headaches or visual disturbances that might suggest a migraine disorder?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headache, tinnitus, hearing loss, nausea, vomiting, or recent respiratory infections. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for clarifying that you have no history of headaches or visual disturbances, which makes a primary vestibular migraine diagnosis less likely given your brief, position-dependent symptoms. To confirm the clinical suspicion of Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV), did the previous physician observe specific eye movements (nystagmus) when you tilted your head back?

REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver.
REQUEST IMAGES: Head_MRI (if symptoms are atypical or if the maneuver is inconclusive).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dix-Hallpike Manoeuvre: Positive for right-sided horizontal nystagmus when moving from sitting to supine position, suggestive of BPPV; MRI Brain: No evidence of central lesions or infarcts.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV), right posterior canal. Based on the positive Dix-Hallpike test with right-sided nystagmus and a normal MRI, I recommend the Epley maneuver for treatment. Would you like me to describe the procedure or schedule a follow-up?
